title: Where do AI agents run when your laptop is closed?
h1: where do ai agents run when your laptop is closed?
description: An AI agent on your laptop stops when the lid closes. The four places it can live instead, what each costs, who looks after it, and which one fits you.
keyword: ai agent running while laptop is closed
keywords: run ai agent while laptop sleeps
answer: nowhere. close the lid and an agent on your laptop stops: the 7am brief doesn't come, your phone can't reach it. to keep it working, it has to live on a computer that stays on. you have three choices: a spare machine at home, a server you rent and babysit, or a hosted computer like dusk cloud that someone else keeps running.

sections.h: why your laptop can't be the home
sections.md:
**an agent is just a program. programs stop when the computer sleeps.**

in Metal you feel it two ways:

- routines don't run while the laptop sleeps or the app is closed. missed by less than 12 hours? it runs once when you're back. longer than that, it's skipped.
- your phone can't reach the bots until the laptop wakes up.

**Settings**, **Remote access**, **Keep this computer awake** helps at your desk. it can't help in a backpack.

**cheap, and it works, until it doesn't.** an old laptop that never sleeps can host your bots for the price of its power.

the catch is you're the ops team. a power cut, a flaky router, an update that reboots it at 3am. if it falls over while you're travelling, nothing runs until someone at home pokes it.

**great if you like servers. a lost weekend if you don't.** [your own server](/docs/your-own-server) is free in Metal. you pay the host.

- ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04, 2 gb of memory or more
- paste one line, wait about ten minutes
- no ports, no domain; the app and server talk through a sealed relay

updates, backups and the bill are yours. use a fresh server, never one holding things you wouldn't hand a bot.

**a computer we host and look after. your bots just keep going.** it has its own storage no one else can reach, backed up every day.

moving takes a minute: pick a plan, sign in under **settings**, **dusk cloud**, and the welcome brings your bots over with their chats, memory and routines. your ai sign-in stays yours. ai usage never lands on the dusk bill.

one honest warning: a bot working around the clock uses your ai plan around the clock. for heavy use, a bigger plan or an api key works out better.

**pick by how much you'll miss the work when the lid's shut.**

- **bots only while you're at your desk?** stay on the laptop. it's free.
- **want the brief before you wake, or replies from your phone at night?** that's the moment to move. most people pick dusk cloud because there's nothing to babysit.
- **you already run servers and enjoy it?** your own server costs you only the server.
- **spare computer that never leaves the house?** fine, as long as it stays on.

you can keep more than one and switch from the top of the sidebar. start on the laptop. move the day a missed routine annoys you.

faq.q: can an ai agent run while my mac is asleep?
faq.a: not on that mac. a sleeping computer runs nothing. keep it awake while plugged in, or move the agent to a computer that stays on.

faq.q: do i need to know linux to keep an agent running 24/7?
faq.a: no. dusk cloud needs no server skills. running [your own server](/docs/your-own-server) is the option that needs some.

faq.q: what happens to my bots if i stop paying for dusk cloud?
faq.a: bots on your own computer carry on. the cloud computer is kept for 30 days after the plan ends, then deleted, and we email you a week before. move your bots back or export a backup first.

faq.q: is it cheaper to run it on my own server?
faq.a: Metal charges nothing for it, so you pay only your hosting company. it's cheaper if your time looking after a server costs you nothing. the [always-on cost calculator](/tools/always-on-cost) puts the numbers side by side.

steps: open **Settings**, **Remote access** and turn on **Keep this computer awake** for tonight
check in the morning whether it ran (**Automations** shows each run)
if it didn't, that's your sign to move it off the laptop

mistakes.mistake: trusting a laptop with a 7am routine
mistakes.fix: a closed lid means no brief. move routines that must run on time.

mistakes.mistake: a cheap server you never update
mistakes.fix: budget an hour a month for it, or don't rent one.

mistakes.mistake: forgetting the ai plan runs all night too
mistakes.fix: watch your usage the first week on an always-on computer.

tip.text: you don't have to choose forever. keep your laptop and add a cloud; switch from the sidebar.
